sentences.text: Wellnhopterus was a mid-sized pterosaur with an estimated wingspan of about 3 meters.
Unlike the slender jaws and long neck of Quetzalcoatlus, this species had a blunt snout and a robust, short neck.
A separate genus named Javelinadactylus was briefly assigned to these fossils in July 2021 before the paper was retracted.
An early reconstruction of Quetzalcoatlus based on these fossils depicted a snout that was too blunt, an error repeated in many popular works.
Its coexistence with larger pterosaurs suggests that pterosaur diversity in the Maastrichtian was higher than previously thought.
Fossils of Wellnhopterus were discovered in March 1986 by preparator Robert Rainey in the Javelina Formation at Big Bend National Park in Brewster County, Texas.
The known fossils include a set of jaws, several neck vertebrae, and a fragmentary long bone.
The species was formally named and described in December 2021 by Brian Andres and Wann Langston Jr.
Only one fossil occurrence of Wellnhopterus has been recorded.
It is likely that Wellnhopterus was a raptorial predator specializing in large prey.
It is classified in the family Azhdarchidae, though its exact position within the group is debated.

A 2023 study by Rubi Pêgas and colleagues recovered Wellnhopterus in a different position than the original 2021 analysis, placing it in a basal position outside the subfamily Quetzalcoatlinae, forming a group with Phosphatodraco and Aralazhdarcho.
Wellnhopterus lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period, specifically between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
This azhdarchid pterosaur lived in what is now Texas, United States.
